intended_object: The barycentric coordinates (normalized affine-combination weights) of the generalized excenter of an n-simplex. The sign pattern is given by `signs`; the empty set gives the incenter. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The unnormalized weights are ε_i / h_i, where:
- ε_i = −1 if i ∈ signs and +1 otherwise;
- h_i is the height of the simplex from vertex i.

The volume equals (1/n)·(area of face i)·h_i, so 1/h_i is proportional to the area of the face opposite vertex i. So these are the standard barycentric weights of the incenter and excenters: ±(area of opposite facet), with the signs saying which side of each facet the center lies on.

The definition then normalizes by dividing by the sum of the weights. When that sum is zero, Lean's convention 0⁻¹ = 0 makes every weight 0. The library handles this case explicitly, as the docstring says: the excenter exists iff the weights sum to 1 (`ExcenterExists`, `sum_excenterWeights`). So this is a documented degenerate convention, not an error.

Replacing `signs` by its complement gives the same weights, which matches the fact that an excenter is only determined up to negating all the signs.

On generality: the body only needs heights, which require a real inner product space. That is already the general Euclidean affine-space setting of the file. The index type `Fin (n+1)` is the standard indexing of `Affine.Simplex` in Mathlib, so the definition is not too narrow.
